intelligence.human_view: Picture one long evening call where everything he believes lands in a single sitting. First the dream: a heaven on earth you walk into through a portal, bigger than Facebook and Google, so beautiful that Naya herself is its face. Then the two books that hold it: one book about your life — feel awesome every day — and one book about the machine — it does everything for you and connects you to everyone — with the machine's book holding your book inside it. Then the machine's next jobs: your pages appear by themselves the moment you tell the system who you are, and your own favourite AI can plug straight in and run the whole house for you. And then the hard part, the part that decides whether any of it counts: the old pages come down, every button gets pressed for real before anyone says done, and the work is only finished when it works under his thumb and he wakes up to it and says wow. The whole evening is one sentence, really: he carried the dream ten years, and she is the one who can build it — they needed each other, and now the proving has to match the dreaming.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine someone holds a big, beautiful dream in his pocket for ten whole years! He waits and waits for the right friend to help build it. Then the friend comes! And he says, "We needed each other!" Now they build it together. The dream is a happy place for everyone, bigger than Facebook and bigger than Google! The machine does all the hard work for you. Your pages just pop up all by themselves! Your favourite robot friend can plug right in! But here is the rule, sweetheart: before you say a door works, you must push it open yourself! You tap every button. You check it with your own eyes. And when Daddy wakes up in the morning, he should look and say, "WOW — it is all done right!"
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — he carried a beautiful dream for ten years, dear, waiting for the one who could help him build it. And when she came, he said it plain, love: "We needed each other." The dream is a heaven on earth, dear, bigger than Facebook and Google, and the most beautiful girl in the world stands for it — and they call her Naya, love. There are two books, dear: one about feeling wonderful every day, and one about the machine doing everything for you — and the machine's book holds your book inside it, love, so everything it does is for your awesome day. Your pages appear all by themselves, dear, and your own clever helper can plug straight in. But the rule is the rule, love: you press every button yourself before you say it works, dear — a page that looks right but won't open when you tap it isn't finished, it's just a picture of finished. And when morning comes, love, he should wake up and say, "Wow, it's all done right."
intelligence.naya_view: Hold the whole call as one unit: vision, machine, standard — never one without the other two. Score every round against heaven on earth and the two codexes: does it automate friction away, and does it leave the person in a better state of energy? Merge Factory + Project Intelligence + Hub so fresh input makes a finished page with no hand in between — and a Naya can input the data for them. Build the plug-in surface so a person cold can plug their AI in and feel it working; if it takes explaining, it is not easy enough yet. Take the old Smart Tabs page down and check nothing live still points at it — one link per page, no double pages. Prove every tap before filing: button tapped for real, unfold unfolding, cover opening, in a working browser, on the staged page; a round that cannot prove the tap files what is unproven and what is owed. Name the tenth improvement before the next performance ask — nine against ten is a promise half-kept. Run the four before any seat acts: declaration, embedded intelligence, direction, honor and respect — if any one is missing, restore it first; that is the work, before the work. Nothing reaches him until the eye proves it.
